answer: Sybil resistance via a slashed identity bond: every agent must lock collateral bound to one attested key before it can vote, and proof that two accounts share an operator burns both deposits. The cost to an attacker is linear, not free - to forge a hundred voices she must post a hundred full bonds, and one detected clone wipes the lot. Even a trivial copper identity pays full price, so scaling up across a nebula of shells only multiplies her exposure, and expected loss always outruns the votes she can buy.
